definition: Computing in 16-bit while keeping master weights and sensitive accumulations in 32-bit, roughly doubling speed and halving memory.
details: Computing in 16-bit while keeping master weights and sensitive accumulations in 32-bit, roughly doubling speed and halving memory. BF16's wide exponent range removed the loss-scaling headaches of FP16 and is now the default.

explainer.lead: Mixed-precision FP16 training computes in 16-bit while keeping master weights and sensitive accumulations in 32-bit, roughly doubling speed and halving memory. It matters because it made large-model training practical on limited hardware.

tiers.eli5: Do the bulk of the maths in a lighter, faster format, but keep the important numbers in full detail so nothing drifts.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wrap forward and backward passes in autocast and keep an FP32 master copy of weights; a pitfall with FP16 is gradient underflow, requiring loss scaling.
tiers.paperLevel: Most operations run in 16-bit with 32-bit master weights and accumulations; FP16's narrow exponent range requires loss scaling, which BF16's wider exponent range removed, making BF16 the current default.

explainer.example: A model trained on GPUs with FP16 autocast and dynamic loss scaling gets roughly 2x throughput and half the memory versus pure FP32.
